authorInfo.bio: John Tyndall (; 2 August 1820 – 4 December 1893) was an Irish physicist. His scientific fame arose in the 1850s from his study of diamagnetism. Later he made discoveries in the realms of infrared radiation and the physical properties of air, proving the connection between atmospheric CO2 and what is now known as the greenhouse effect in 1859.

sourceTitle: Hours of Exercise in the Alps
description: "Hours of Exercise in the Alps" by John Tyndall is a collection of travel narratives and reflections on mountaineering written in the late 19th century. The work recounts the author’s personal adventures in the majestic alpine landscape while exploring both the physical challenges of climbing and the profound connection with nature that these experiences foster.
